methods.label: Use equal-radius triangles
methods.explanation:
The radii satisfy \(OA=OB=OC\), so \(\triangle AOB\) and \(\triangle BOC\) are isosceles. This lets us find their angles at \(B\) from the given angles at \(O\).

The two base angles of each isosceles triangle are equal, and its three angles sum to \(180^\circ\). Hence
\[
\angle ABO=\frac{180^\circ-140^\circ}{2}=20^\circ,
\]
\[
\angle OBC=\frac{180^\circ-120^\circ}{2}=30^\circ.
\]
In the displayed configuration, ray \(BO\) lies inside \(\angle ABC\), so these two angles add:
\[
\angle ABC=20^\circ+30^\circ=\boxed{50^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
